resources.string: What this app declares, what the system actually allows, and a saved reference to return to

Two different things decide what an app can do. A manifest permission is what the app asked for — the system may or may not have granted it. An app op is what the system actually allows right now: allowed, ignored, restricted to foreground use, or the override removed so the manifest decides again. Modern Android moves more control into app ops every release, including things no manifest permission covers at all — the clipboard, vibration, background execution — so showing only one of the two would be a half answer that looks complete. Writing an app op needs root here (or ADB through Shizuku, which this app does not run yet), and every write is read back afterwards so you are told what the device actually accepted instead of what we sent. The saved reference is the answer to a real problem: reinstalling an app or switching ROM restores every permission. Save the reference once, compare later, and see exactly which ops drifted.
